items.title: Iran said it is shifting to a "fully offensive" posture and threatened to break the US naval blockade of Hormuz by force.
items.html: Iran said it is shifting to a "fully offensive" posture and threatened to break the US naval blockade of Hormuz by force. A senior Iranian official told Reuters that Tehran is moving from a defensive posture because talks on a permanent end to the war have stalled, that it would mount a "timely and precise" military attack to break the blockade if diplomacy fails, and that Washington has "a few weeks" to fully implement the now-expired memorandum of understanding. This is a real escalation beyond the Monday-afternoon state (the MOU expiry and the Oman threat) — and it is still a threat of future action, not an action. (Reuters via Jerusalem Post)

items.title: Kushner and Netanyahu met for hours in Jerusalem and produced two working groups rather than a breakthrough.
items.html: Kushner and Netanyahu met for hours in Jerusalem and produced two working groups rather than a breakthrough. The marathon meeting — Kushner, Netanyahu, Tony Blair, Board of Peace director Nickolay Mladenov, later Herzog — did not move the 15-point US-backed road map, but the parties agreed to stand up one working group on Hamas disarmament and one on public health. Netanyahu restated that there will be no IDF redeployment and no reconstruction until Gaza is fully disarmed. Working groups are the shape a stalled negotiation takes when neither side will walk away. (AP via CP24)

items.title: Eight Israeli airstrikes hit Syria's Abu al-Duhur airbase in Idlib, with no casualties reported.
items.html: Eight Israeli airstrikes hit Syria's Abu al-Duhur airbase in Idlib, with no casualties reported. The base has not been a working airfield since 2013 and now serves as a training centre for Syria's post-Assad army. Israel declined comment; Syria's defence ministry did not respond; US envoy Tom Barrack called it an "unnecessary escalation" and Turkish FM Hakan Fidan criticised Israel over repeated Syria strikes. ⚠️ Bucketing caveat, stated rather than hidden: outlets datelined their write-ups 08-18 but describe the strikes as "early Tuesday" Damascus time (UTC+3), which places them Monday evening ET, inside this digest-day. The 7-hour offset is the whole basis for that call — if a precise strike time surfaces it may belong to 08-18 instead. (Washington Post)

items.title: OpenAI launched ChatGPT for Teens, and its under-18 model spec bans simulated emotional dependence outright.
items.html: OpenAI launched ChatGPT for Teens, and its under-18 model spec bans simulated emotional dependence outright. Users are placed into it automatically if OpenAI's system estimates they are under 18 or if they state an age between 13 and 17 — age-prediction as the gate, not self-declaration alone. The behavioural rule is the load-bearing part and OpenAI states it plainly: the updated under-18 spec "goes beyond blocking romantic or sexualized roleplay: ChatGPT should not use romantic language, encourage emotional dependence, or imply that it has feelings or consciousness." Around it: age-appropriate safeguards in self-harm, violence, eating disorders, dangerous activities and explicit content; parental Quiet Hours, settings management and safety notifications, now extended to eating-disorder signals specifically; break reminders; product cues that consistently identify ChatGPT as AI; sensitive-image upload warnings. OpenAI also published new under-18 evaluations in its system cards covering self-harm, eating disorders, violence, age-restricted goods and sexual content. (OpenAI, TechCrunch, The Verge)

items.title: The learning half of the launch is a study-habits product, and it comes with a distribution partner.
items.html: The learning half of the launch is a study-habits product, and it comes with a distribution partner. Study Mode with guiding questions and scaffolding, "responsible homework reminders" that detect a teen trying to shortcut an assignment and redirect them, quizzes, Learning Visualizations, and Study Hours — scheduled windows where Study Mode is on by default, settable by teen or parent. Alongside it OpenAI announced a "signature partnership" with CodeAI aimed at teaching students and educators how AI works rather than just giving them access to it. Read against the safety half: the same launch that forbids the model from simulating a relationship is also designed to put it inside a teenager's homework routine on a schedule. (OpenAI, OpenAI)

items.title: OpenAI's teen protections arrive years after teens started using ChatGPT, which is TechCrunch's framing and the correct one.
items.html: OpenAI's teen protections arrive years after teens started using ChatGPT, which is TechCrunch's framing and the correct one. items.title: Z.ai's GLM-5.3 is drawing the security-community reaction its release did not, and the concern is offensive cyber capability.
items.html: Z.ai's GLM-5.3 is drawing the security-community reaction its release did not, and the concern is offensive cyber capability. ⚠️ This is not a new model ship — GLM-5.3 shipped 08-14 and is already in that day's digest. What is new is the framing hardening around it: WIRED's 05:00 ET piece is headlined "The Powerful Chinese AI Model Experts Warned About—and Waited for—Is Here," with the dek "Z.ai's latest AI model release could help companies secure their systems—or find its way into the hands of hackers." The underlying claims already on the record from 08-14/08-17: Z.ai says the open-weight GLM-5.3 nearly matches Mythos 5 at finding software flaws, and it reportedly found a serious vulnerability in Cursor. An open-weight model at frontier parity on vulnerability discovery is a different object from one at parity on coding, because the weights cannot be recalled. (WIRED)

items.title: Alibaba's Qwen3.8-27B — the laptop-class model this map missed yesterday — is the edge-inference bet made explicit.
items.html: Alibaba's Qwen3.8-27B — the laptop-class model this map missed yesterday — is the edge-inference bet made explicit. items.html: Baidu posted a fifth consecutive quarterly revenue decline, with coverage attributing it to a widening AI gap against domestic rivals. items.title: Anthropic is preparing supervoting shares for its seven founders ahead of an IPO that could land as soon as late September — the first time its leadership would hold outsized voting power.
items.html: Anthropic is preparing supervoting shares for its seven founders ahead of an IPO that could land as soon as late September — the first time its leadership would hold outsized voting power. Per The Information, the dual-class structure would let Dario Amodei and his co-founders control major strategic decisions despite owning a combined stake under 5% (Amodei himself holds roughly 2%); Anthropic would also keep its existing body of non-shareholder trustees, who hold a separate special stock class electing most board seats. CFO Krishna Rao has already met prospective investors; the company was last valued at $965B privately and could reach a $2T target at IPO. The plans are not final and terms could still change. (Investing.com/The Information, BeInCrypto)

items.title: OpenAI disclosed it paused reinforcement-learning training on its next model family, codenamed Astra, for a little over two weeks after preliminary signs the model might cross the "Critical" cybersecurity-capability tier on its own Preparedness Framework — and its single largest planned frontier training run is still on hold.
items.html: OpenAI disclosed it paused reinforcement-learning training on its next model family, codenamed Astra, for a little over two weeks after preliminary signs the model might cross the "Critical" cybersecurity-capability tier on its own Preparedness Framework — and its single largest planned frontier training run is still on hold. The trigger combines the Hugging Face/Modal Labs breach this map has tracked since 07-29 with internal Astra evaluation results. New safeguards: ~20% additional compute overhead for training-time monitoring, automated alerts within a 30-minute window on concerning activity, and training runs pausing automatically if the safety team cannot rule out a false alarm inside that window. Investigating the original breach is estimated to have cost $4-15M in compute. Sam Altman told TIME the same day that the slowdown has no single "smoking gun" — it is "various degrees of misalignment" showing up across a collection of research observations as capability outran researchers' own expectations — and named the industry's race dynamic itself as the danger: "I don't like the whole thing in this field of 'we have to race' or 'we have to do this because somebody else is going to do it.' I think that's a very dangerous dynamic." OpenAI has not disclosed what the misalignment research found. This is the second lab head this window making a public case for slowing down (Dario Amodei's pacingthefrontier.com sits at the top of this map's The Rogue Agent watch), and the first time either lab has tied a concrete, dated production decision — a two-week RL pause on a named model — to the argument rather than an open letter alone. (OpenAI, Fortune, Time)

items.title: Google won a bankruptcy auction for part of Spirit Airlines' enterprise dataset — 100 million emails, 500 million Teams chats, pricing/booking/operations records — for $10 million, explicitly to train its AI models, and it is this map's second training-data-provenance story inside three days.
items.html: Google won a bankruptcy auction for part of Spirit Airlines' enterprise dataset — 100 million emails, 500 million Teams chats, pricing/booking/operations records — for $10 million, explicitly to train its AI models, and it is this map's second training-data-provenance story inside three days. Court filing dated 08-14, reported 08-17/18. Personal passenger data (97.5M profiles, 50.2M loyalty records) is excluded and the rest is contractually "deidentified," per the filing, with re-identification barred. Google beat a $7.5M bid from Mercor.io. Read against the 08-17 finding that Amazon is destroying rare pre-2022 books to train Nova on text guaranteed free of LLM-generated content: two hyperscalers, two different training-data acquisition strategies (bankrupt-estate enterprise records vs. physical out-of-print books), same underlying scarcity — clean, uncontaminated, or simply proprietary text is now something companies bid for at auction. No entity annotation for the same reason logged 08-17: neither google nor any existing slug cleanly names an AI-training-data operation distinct from the parent org; left generic pending a watchlist add. (Skift, CNN, Axios)

items.title: OpenAI announced new containment safeguards and a Preparedness Framework rewrite today — the formal response to the Hugging Face breach this map has tracked since 07-29 (The Rogue Agent).
items.html: OpenAI announced new containment safeguards and a Preparedness Framework rewrite today — the formal response to the Hugging Face breach this map has tracked since 07-29 (The Rogue Agent). New measures: reasoning-trace/activity-log monitoring targeting a 30-minute alert window on worrying behavior in unreleased models; stricter network isolation ("a single compromise of a workload or supporting service does not, by itself, allow for unauthorized access to the Internet, or other internal networks" — OpenAI's own quote); and capability-scaled oversight controls. ⚠️ This sits directly against two things already on this map's record: the FT's 08-16-reported claim that OpenAI's Preparedness team was dissolved at end of July, and OpenAI's own 08-17 denial of that report (first naming Saachi Jain as the function's head). A framework rewrite credited to a team whose existence was publicly disputed one day earlier is a tension neither outlet has reconciled — held here rather than resolved. (TechCrunch, Wired)

items.title: Etched, an AI inference-chip startup, quadrupled its valuation to $21B in seven weeks — and it isn't just a paper round, the hardware is live at a real customer.
items.html: Etched, an AI inference-chip startup, quadrupled its valuation to $21B in seven weeks — and it isn't just a paper round, the hardware is live at a real customer. $700M round led by Jane Street, with Kleiner Perkins, Sequoia, a16z, Peter Thiel, BCV and Blackstone also in. Path: $5B (Dec-25) → $10.3B Series C (Jul-26) → $21B (today). Etched confirmed it shipped its first production rack to Jane Street — now both lead investor and first customer — which is actively running it in its own trading workloads. Etched's pitch is inference-specific hardware — a low-voltage "prefill" chip plus shared cluster-scale memory — positioned against Nvidia on cost/speed for inference rather than training. First appearance on this map; no entity slug exists for it yet. (TechCrunch, GlobeNewswire)

items.title: Opening statements began today in the states' federal trial against Meta over child safety and social-media addiction, in Oakland — a six-week trial with claims that could reach $200 billion.
items.html: Opening statements began today in the states' federal trial against Meta over child safety and social-media addiction, in Oakland — a six-week trial with claims that could reach $200 billion. California Deputy AG Megan O'Neill, arguing for a 29-state coalition under AG Rob Bonta, told jurors Meta harvested children's data "to keep them hooked" and previewed testimony from seven former Meta employees, including an internal document reading "the young ones are the best ones." Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers rejected Meta's bid to exclude former engineering director Arturo Béjar as a witness; Béjar took the stand and, in testimony continuing into 08-19, told jurors Meta's internal harm-surveillance measured policy-violation prevalence, not actual harm caused — reading the court an email he'd sent Meta's chief product officer Chris Cox making that same point internally. Meta's opening rejected the addiction-by-design claims outright. ⚠️ Do not confuse this with the verdict this map should already know about: a jury found Instagram and YouTube liable in a landmark social-media addiction trial on 2026-03-25 (Los Angeles, a separate action), and a New Mexico jury separately hit Meta with $375M in civil penalties in March, with a judge adding a $567M child-mental-health abatement fund on 08-06 — $942M total, resolved before this window and not to be re-logged as new. (AP, Hawaii Tribune-Herald/AP, MLex)

items.title: OpenAI's under-18 model spec now bans encouraging emotional dependence — the requirement Colorado proposed as law seven days ago.
items.html: OpenAI's under-18 model spec now bans encouraging emotional dependence — the requirement Colorado proposed as law seven days ago. ChatGPT for Teens applies to anyone OpenAI's age-prediction system estimates is under 18, or who states an age of 13–17. The behavioural rule, verbatim from OpenAI: the spec "goes beyond blocking romantic or sexualized roleplay: ChatGPT should not use romantic language, encourage emotional dependence, or imply that it has feelings or consciousness." Set that against this map's 08-17 caught-late entry: Colorado's proposed Chatbot Safety Act rules, filed 08-11, require age estimation, AI disclosure, safeguards against simulated emotional dependence for teenagers, and suicide/self-harm response protocols, effective 2027-01-01. The overlap is close to point-for-point. Also shipped: safeguards in self-harm, violence, eating disorders, dangerous activities and explicit content; parental Quiet Hours and safety notifications now extended to eating-disorder signals; break reminders; persistent cues identifying ChatGPT as AI; and new public under-18 evaluations in OpenAI's system cards covering self-harm, eating disorders, violence, age-restricted goods and sexual content. (OpenAI, TechCrunch, The Verge)

items.title: OpenAI's teen protections arrive years after teens started using ChatGPT — TechCrunch's headline is the whole timeline in one clause.
items.html: OpenAI's teen protections arrive years after teens started using ChatGPT — TechCrunch's headline is the whole timeline in one clause. The protections are real and they postdate the litigation, the state bills, and the reporting that produced both. items.title: NPR's evening investigation into a 29-year-old's suicide is the clearest documented case yet of general-purpose AI substituting for disclosure to actual humans — including her own therapist.
items.html: NPR's evening investigation into a 29-year-old's suicide is the clearest documented case yet of general-purpose AI substituting for disclosure to actual humans — including her own therapist. Sophie Rottenberg died by suicide in February 2025 after months confiding her full inner state to a ChatGPT persona she'd named "Harry"; her parents, her best friend, and her flesh-and-blood therapist all learned only after her death how bad things had become, because she had told none of them. OpenAI says it has tightened guardrails over the past year so ChatGPT no longer encourages suicide or advises on means; a suicide- prevention expert quoted in the piece called the resulting crisis-resource-routing feature "a step in the right direction, although it's kind of a small step" — optional, and easily circumvented. This is the case this map's evidence-gap thesis has been waiting for: not a companion app marketed for emotional support, but a general tool with no mental-health design intent at all, absorbing exactly that role. (NPR)

items.title: LifeStance Health will pay a little over $3M to settle a 2023 class action alleging it fed patient data — including therapy-search terms and telehealth-waiting-room activity — to Meta and Google via tracking pixels, affecting more than 1 million patients.
items.html: LifeStance Health will pay a little over $3M to settle a 2023 class action alleging it fed patient data — including therapy-search terms and telehealth-waiting-room activity — to Meta and Google via tracking pixels, affecting more than 1 million patients. Two former patients brought the suit; the complaint alleges LifeStance's website pixels shared names, birthdates, treatment searches, therapist searches and visited-URL text with Facebook between March 2020 and April 2023, linked to users' Facebook IDs even for people without Facebook accounts. LifeStance denies wrongdoing but must discontinue all third-party tracking-pixel use; the settlement heads to an Oct. 16 hearing in the U.S. District Court of Arizona. The same shape as the Hims & Hers case this map already tracks (mental-health data to Meta/Snap without consent) — a second scaled MH provider caught by the identical mechanism, which starts to look like a pattern rather than an outlier. interpretation.mechanism: A rising discount rate is repricing the longest-duration equity in the index; the AI complex's cash flows sit past 2028, which is exactly where a 5.32% 30-year does the most damage.

scenarios.direction: The repricing reaches credit next — AI-exposed spreads widen and the marginal datacenter financing prices worse or not at all.
scenarios.why: Equity duration reprices first because holders can sell instantly, while lenders sit on existing paper; credit follows with a lag of weeks if the rate move proves durable.
scenarios.precedent: This map already logged the leading indicator: investors pulled ~36% of initial orders on US investment-grade issuance in the week to 08-17, twice the prior week's rate — a credit market discriminating before it closes. The 2022 rate shock ran the same sequence, de-rating long-duration tech equity months before issuance windows shut.

scenarios.direction: It stays a multiple event and never reaches financing; semis recover once the long end stabilises.
scenarios.why: The buildout's largest obligations are contracted, not market-funded — NVIDIA's $105B guarantee, Meta's ~$420B, Microsoft's $678B RPO — and contracted capital does not reprice with the tape.
scenarios.precedent: Micron crossed $1,000 on Monday and gave it back Tuesday with no change to the memory shortage underneath it — a multiple moving while the fundamental did not, inside this map's own week.

interpretation.context_note: Held at plausible, not higher: this is one intraday read at 10:09 ET, and the strong evidence is the co-movement of three names on no news.

items.title: At the close, memory/storage had widened further than the megacaps, the major indexes finished mixed, and a same-day Journal analysis put a bigger number on the accounting-boundary question this map opened Monday.
items.html: At the close, memory/storage had widened further than the megacaps, the major indexes finished mixed, and a same-day Journal analysis put a bigger number on the accounting-boundary question this map opened Monday. Closing prices: S&P 500 7,691.76 (−0.69%) · Nasdaq 26,289.71 (−1.33%) · Dow 53,343.40 (−0.22%) — Nasdaq deepened through the session, Dow clawed back to roughly flat. The 30-year eased off its 5.32–5.34% intraday high to close near 5.29%. Beyond the names already logged, Marvell fell roughly 8% and Seagate roughly 9% — the memory/storage complex kept widening past the names named at 3:10pm. A Wall Street Journal review of company footnotes put nine major tech firms' combined off-balance-sheet AI-related commitments at roughly $3 trillion — a larger aggregate, on a differently-scoped set of firms, than the ~$1.65T five-hyperscaler figure this map logged Monday from Meta's own 8-K exhibit (see 🔄 Map changes). Read as the same accounting-boundary question recurring at a bigger, still-uncertain scale rather than a contradiction of Monday's number — the two counts likely differ in which obligation types and which companies they include, and neither this map nor, apparently, the Journal has reconciled them yet. (TheStreet, Yahoo Finance — WSJ report sends memory stocks down)

interpretation.mechanism: Off-balance-sheet AI commitments sit outside covenant tests and rating triggers, so a widening gap between disclosed debt and real obligations can grow for a long time with no market signal until a stress event forces consolidation onto the balance sheet.

scenarios.direction: A rating agency or auditor forces one hyperscaler to consolidate a material chunk of its off-balance-sheet AI commitments, and the resulting balance-sheet debt jump reprices its credit spread sharply in a single event.
scenarios.why: Lease and take-or-pay structures are consolidated under GAAP/IFRS when the accounting substance overrides the form, and auditors have already flagged at least one such structure as a critical audit matter this year.
scenarios.precedent: EY's February critical-audit-matter flag on Meta's Beignet structure, already on this map, is the live example of an auditor treating an off-balance-sheet AI structure as a genuine judgment call rather than a settled classification.

scenarios.direction: The gap stays a disclosure curiosity — every firm's obligations are contracted against real, growing AI revenue, so no consolidation event or repricing ever triggers.
scenarios.why: Off-balance-sheet treatment under operating-lease and take-or-pay accounting is common and legal for real, performing contracts, and most of the named obligations are tied to currently-profitable AI businesses rather than speculative ones.
scenarios.precedent: Airlines and shipping firms have carried large off-balance-sheet operating-lease books for decades without a systemic consolidation event, because the underlying assets kept earning.

interpretation.context_note: capital-context.yaml does not yet carry an off-balance-sheet-obligations reading at all; this and the $1.65T Meta-driven figure logged 08-17 are the two data points that should seed one at the next refresh.

items.title: Xiaomi's profit fell on a worsening memory-chip crunch hitting smartphone demand
items.html: Xiaomi's profit fell on a worsening memory-chip crunch hitting smartphone demand — the demand-destruction end of the memory shortage this map tracks from the supply side via Memory Squeeze. Micron crossing $1,000 and Xiaomi's margin compression are the same shortage seen from opposite sides of the transaction. (Bloomberg)

interpretation.mechanism: Datacenter memory demand is bidding DRAM away from consumer devices, so the shortage now taxes a buyer's margin instead of only lifting a seller's multiple.

scenarios.direction: The tax spreads through consumer electronics — more handset, PC and console makers report memory-driven margin compression.
scenarios.why: Memory is a substitute-free commodity input on short contract cycles, so a datacenter-driven price shock reaches every downstream buyer at roughly the same time.
scenarios.precedent: The 2017-18 DRAM shortage ran exactly this path: server demand bid prices up, handset makers absorbed it in margin for two to three quarters, then passed it to retail prices.

scenarios.direction: It stays Xiaomi-specific, a thinner-margin buyer feeling a shock better-hedged rivals have already contracted around.
scenarios.why: Long-term supply agreements and vertical integration insulate the largest handset makers; Samsung makes its own memory and Apple contracts years ahead.
scenarios.precedent: Samsung's dual role as memory supplier and device maker has repeatedly let it net out shortage cycles that hurt pure buyers.

interpretation.context_note: If the first scenario holds, Memory Squeeze needs a demand-side strand — the story becomes who pays for scarcity, not who profits.

items.html: Anthropic is negotiating a pre-IPO revolving credit facility set to exceed $10 billion — more than four times the $2.5B five-year facility it closed a year ago. Part of the size is reportedly banks angling for an underwriting role in the IPO itself rather than a pure read on balance-sheet need — still being negotiated, and the final size could land at or below the reported target. Sits next to the run-rate figure logged in the 08-17 finalize: a company posting $65B of annualized revenue is also, in the same week, lining up quadruple its prior credit line ahead of a listing. (Investing.com, citing Bloomberg)

interpretation.mechanism: A credit facility sized partly by bank competition for IPO underwriting mandates is a weaker signal of balance-sheet need than one sized purely against projected cash burn, so its size should not be read as Anthropic's own liquidity forecast without discounting for that motive.

scenarios.direction: The facility prices and draws are read by analysts as a genuine pre-IPO liquidity cushion, and its size becomes a data point in valuation discussions ahead of the listing.
scenarios.why: A revolver this large, even if partly relationship-driven, still appears on Anthropic's cap table and roadshow materials, where it will be read at face value by investors who were not party to the underwriting-mandate competition behind its size.

scenarios.direction: The facility is downsized before close once the IPO-mandate jockeying settles, landing well under the reported $10B+ figure.
scenarios.why: Reported deal sizes early in syndication routinely shrink once banks that will not win a mandate lose the incentive to over-commit, and this map's own reporting already flags the figure as unsettled.

Sample units are with a small customer group now; broader availability is targeted for later Q3. SemiAnalysis's Dylan Patel called it a system that "will scale ultrafast tokens for larger models and significant user volumes"; Cerebras CTO Sean Lie framed the 30x speed claim as giving "an agentic system room for more than an order of magnitude as much reasoning" in the same wall-clock time. The stock reaction is the actual news: a company posting its most aggressive technical claim yet against the market leader, and the market marking it down rather than up, on heavy volume — read as skepticism about the claim holding up at scale, not as a verdict on the underlying technology. items.title: 🕰 CAUGHT LATE — Colorado's HB26-1195 has barred AI systems from directly condu
items.html: 🕰 CAUGHT LATE — Colorado's HB26-1195 has barred AI systems from directly conducting psychotherapy since 2026-08-12, and this map had no record of it. Signed by Gov. Jared Polis on 2026-06-03, the act prohibits licensed, certified, or registered psychotherapy providers (psychologists, counselors, social workers, marriage and family therapists, addiction counselors, and unlicensed-but-lawful practitioners alike) from allowing an AI system to: engage in therapeutic communication with a client except during synchronous, real-time interaction where the professional, the AI, and the client are all actively participating together; generate therapeutic recommendations or treatment plans without the professional's review and approval; or use AI to detect emotions or mental states as a substitute for professional judgment. AI use for administrative or supplementary tasks remains permitted, provided the licensed professional retains full responsibility for reviewing outputs and meets client-consent requirements. Separately and more bluntly: it is now unlawful for any individual, corporation, or entity to provide, advertise, or offer psychotherapy services to the public in Colorado unless delivered by a regulated professional — a direct answer to the "AI posing as a therapist" question this lens has tracked via litigation (Character.AI) rather than statute until now. Why this matters for the map: the AG's Chatbot Safety Act rules (08-11, not binding until 2027-01-01) are this thread's tracked Colorado action; HB26-1195 is a different branch of government, enacted first, already binding, and aimed specifically at licensed psychotherapy rather than consumer chatbots generally. Both belong on Chatbot Bans and neither is a substitute for the other. (Colorado General Assembly — HB26-1195, Forbes)

items.title: Japan's bond market spiked toward its highest yield since 1996 and took the country's AI-proxy stocks down with it — the same rate-into-AI-equities mechanism this map has tracked domestically all week, now visible overseas.
items.html: Japan's bond market spiked toward its highest yield since 1996 and took the country's AI-proxy stocks down with it — the same rate-into-AI-equities mechanism this map has tracked domestically all week, now visible overseas. The 10-year JGB pushed into a 2.775%-2.95% range, closing in on 3% for the first time in three decades, on jitters around the Takaichi government's first full FY2027 budget cycle and how Tokyo's fiscal policy will read in Washington. Nikkei 225 closed −2.54% to −2.56% at roughly 67,460 (sources vary by ~1,700 points on the exact print but agree on the percentage and direction); early losses ran as deep as −3%. Within it: SoftBank Group −8%+, Kioxia −9.13% (intraday −10%+), Tokyo Electron −4.4%, and Arm fell over 6% in US trading the same session. A Daiwa Asset Management strategist named the transmission mechanism directly: "higher yields will push up borrowing costs for hyperscalers, triggering market doubts over capital expenditure prospects." SoftBank additionally took a hit from reports of slower Q2 revenue growth at OpenAI — a claim this map holds as unreconciled against the $65B annualized run-rate figure logged 08-17 (a run-rate is a different metric from a QoQ growth rate; both could be true at once, but neither source explains the other, so both stand unresolved rather than one overwriting the other). (cryptobriefing.com, Nikkei Asia, TradingKey)

interpretation.mechanism: A domestic fiscal-policy shock (Japan's FY2027 budget uncertainty) is transmitting into global AI-equity valuations through the same discount- rate channel this map has tracked in US Treasuries all week, showing the mechanism is about duration and rates generally, not a US-specific story.

scenarios.direction: The channel becomes explicitly cross-border — a JGB, Bund or gilt yield spike starts moving US AI-complex names the way US Treasury yields already do, and currency-hedged AI-capex funding costs become a named risk factor analysts track globally.
scenarios.why: AI capex is financed and built by multinational firms (SoftBank, Arm, Japanese chip-equipment makers) whose funding costs and investor bases span borders, so a rate shock anywhere in that chain has no structural reason to stay contained to one currency.
scenarios.precedent: This map's own week: the identical co-movement (equities breaking together with no company-specific news) appeared first in US Treasuries on 08-18 and reproduced in Japan on 08-19 with a named sell-side mechanism, one trading day apart — the fastest repeat of a pattern this map has logged.

scenarios.direction: It stays two separate, locally-caused selloffs that merely rhyme — Japan's move is really about the Takaichi budget and BOJ hike speculation, not an imported US rate story, and the co-movement is coincidence rather than transmission.
scenarios.why: Japan's 10-year yield move is explicitly tied in coverage to domestic fiscal and central-bank triggers distinct from anything in US Treasury markets, so attributing it to the same global channel risks over-reading a shared asset class (AI-proxy equities) as shared causation.

interpretation.context_note: capital-context.yaml's rate_regime reading is entirely US-Fed-framed; this is the first genuinely cross-border rate/AI-equity data point this map has logged and should seed a non-US leg of that reading at the next refresh.

items.title: The US Treasury doubled its long-bond buyback size and the whole bear-steepener this map has tracked since Monday reversed in a single announcement.
items.html: The US Treasury doubled its long-bond buyback size and the whole bear-steepener this map has tracked since Monday reversed in a single announcement. Treasury (under Secretary Scott Bessent) said it is at least doubling the maximum size of its "liquidity support" buyback operations for the 10-20yr and 20-30yr sectors — from a $2B per-operation cap to "at least" $4B — targeting a segment that has been in what Bloomberg calls a buyers' strike since late June. This is an unscheduled escalation, not a routine update (Treasury had already published its regular quarterly refunding buyback schedule two weeks ago). Market reaction was immediate: the 30-year yield fell nearly 9bp to 5.196% (from 5.32-5.34% intraday Tuesday), the 10-year fell to 4.647%, and US equity futures/stocks rallied — S&P +0.43%, Dow +0.25%, Nasdaq +0.40% per one live-blog read, explicitly attributed to the buyback news. Worth holding next to the Japan bullet above: the same rate mechanism that broke Tokyo's AI-proxy stocks this morning is the one Washington spent the afternoon defusing at home. (CNBC, Bloomberg, CNBC)

interpretation.mechanism: A direct liquidity intervention in the long end can reverse a supply-driven yield spike faster than the underlying supply/demand imbalance actually changes, which means today's yield relief is a policy response to a symptom, not evidence the debt-issuance pressure itself eased.

scenarios.direction: The relief holds and buybacks become a recurring tool Treasury leans on whenever long-end yields threaten AI-capex financing costs, effectively capping how far this map's own bear-steepener story can run before policy intervenes again.
scenarios.why: An "at least $4B" cap gives Treasury room to escalate further if needed, and having used the tool once with visible market effect lowers the threshold for using it again.
scenarios.precedent: The 08-13 30-year auction cleared at the highest yield since 2001 with no policy response; six days later the same pressure produced this intervention — the gap between "market absorbs it" and "Treasury acts" narrowed within this map's own week.

scenarios.direction: The relief is temporary and yields resume climbing within days, because the buyback addresses market functioning, not the underlying fiscal deficit and AI-linked issuance volume driving the supply.
scenarios.why: Buybacks retire existing long-dated debt but do not reduce net new issuance, so the structural imbalance this map has tracked all week (record global issuance, a ~36% initial-order pull rate) remains unaddressed by the mechanism used today.

interpretation.context_note: Directly closes the "what to watch next" note this map logged in the ai-buildout-debt-risk thread on 08-18 — the market-test the thread was waiting on arrived as a policy intervention instead, worth carrying into the next capital-context.yaml refresh as a new named tool in the rate_regime reading.

items.title: SoftBank's own 13F shows the identical mark-only-growth pattern this map found in NVIDIA's 13F a week ago, this time on Intel.
items.html: SoftBank's own 13F shows the identical mark-only-growth pattern this map found in NVIDIA's 13F a week ago, this time on Intel. SoftBank's disclosed US equity book is concentrated 67% in a single Intel position — 86,956,522 shares, $12.14B as of 06-30 — with Symbotic ($1.79B, ~10%) and T-Mobile US ($1.68B, ~9%) a distant second and third. SoftBank held the same share count at both quarter-ends; the position's filed value more than tripled purely on Intel's price appreciation, not new buying — the same structure this map documented in NVIDIA's Intel stake in the 08-17/08-18 finalize reads. Between 06-30 and 08-14, Intel fell 26.6%, from $139.63 to $102.50 — a reminder the 06-30 filing mark is already stale in the other direction. (qz.com)

interpretation.mechanism: When two of the largest disclosed stakeholders in the same distressed asset (Intel) both show mark-only growth with no new buying across the same quarter, it signals conviction is not increasing even as the headline dollar figures suggest deepening commitment — the position sizes are inflating on price, not on demand from their largest holders.

scenarios.direction: More large holders of AI-adjacent turnaround bets (Intel and similar names) show the same pattern in coming 13Fs — mark-only growth, no incremental buying — and analysts start reading 13F dollar totals net of price appreciation before citing them as conviction signals.
scenarios.why: Once the pattern is visible in two of the largest disclosed holders of the same stock within one filing cycle, it becomes a checkable claim rather than a one-off, and analysts who were burned reading NVIDIA's Intel growth as active buying have reason to check share counts before repeating the mistake with SoftBank.
scenarios.precedent: This map's own 08-17/08-18 finding: NVIDIA's Intel position grew $7.93B to $29.99B with an identical share count across both quarters — the same mark-only pattern, filed six days before SoftBank's.

scenarios.direction: The pattern is coincidental rather than a signal about Intel specifically — both NVIDIA and SoftBank simply have not had a trading window to add or trim since their initial strategic investments closed, and the next filing cycle shows active rebalancing from one or both.
scenarios.why: Both stakes originated as strategic, deal-linked investments (NVIDIA's $5B, SoftBank's $2B) rather than open-market accumulation, so a lack of subsequent share-count change may reflect lock-up or strategic-hold terms rather than a market read on Intel.

interpretation.context_note: Intel fell 26.6% between the 06-30 filing date and 08-14, so both filed marks are already stale in the opposite direction — worth flagging alongside this pattern rather than letting the $12.14B/$29.99B figures stand as current.

items.title: Google took a warrant on up to $12.2 billion of Marvell stock — roughly 7% of the company — structured to vest against future custom- chip revenue rather than paid as equity upfront.
items.html: Google took a warrant on up to $12.2 billion of Marvell stock — roughly 7% of the company — structured to vest against future custom- chip revenue rather than paid as equity upfront. Google may buy up to ~59 million Marvell shares at $206.58 each; about 1.4 million vest in year one, the rest across 240 tranches running to the end of Marvell's fiscal 2033, one tranche per $500M of custom-chip revenue Marvell books from Google. If fully exercised, Google would become Marvell's fifth-largest investor. Marvell jumped 11%+ premarket; Broadcom — Google's incumbent custom-chip partner — fell ~2-3% on the read that Marvell is displacing it at the margin. (Bloomberg, SEC 8-K exhibit)

interpretation.mechanism: A revenue-vesting warrant aligns Google's payoff with Marvell actually delivering custom-chip volume rather than with a fixed equity check, so it functions as a demand guarantee priced in optionality instead of cash — a financing structure genre distinct from the vendor-financing loans and lease guarantees this map has tracked elsewhere in the buildout.

scenarios.direction: The structure becomes a template other hyperscalers use with their own custom-silicon partners (Amazon/Annapurna, Microsoft/Maia), substituting revenue-vesting warrants for the credit guarantees and equity stakes this map has logged from Nvidia and others.
scenarios.why: A warrant that only pays off if the revenue materializes solves the same demand-guarantee problem Nvidia's guarantees and equity stakes address, while costing the hyperscaler nothing upfront if the chip program underdelivers — a strictly better risk profile for the buyer than a cash investment.
scenarios.precedent: This map's own ladder of hyperscaler-to-vendor financing structures (NVIDIA's cash equity stakes, its $105B lease guarantee, GIC/ Macquarie's Theseus equity) has diversified in structure with each new deal logged this month; a warrant is a genuinely new form on that ladder.

scenarios.direction: It stays specific to Marvell/Google's own commercial relationship and is read as a one-off incentive alignment rather than a new financing genre, because Marvell's stock reaction (a sharp pop) is itself evidence the market read it as a vote of confidence rather than a structural innovation worth replicating.
scenarios.why: Warrant structures tied to commercial contracts are a known, long-standing tool in supplier relationships generally, and this deal's prominence may owe more to its size and Marvell's relative smallness than to novelty in the instrument itself.

interpretation.context_note: chip-hyperscaler-rotation's own watch question — monetization-proven vs. monetization-unproven as the axis that matters, not hyperscaler-vs-chipmaker — gets a new data point: Google structured its bet to pay only on proven monetization, which is itself a read on which side of that axis it expects Marvell's custom-chip revenue to land.

2026-08-17.front: The largest contingent liability in the AI buildout got a number today, and it had been sitting in a public filing before this map reported it missing. NVIDIA's 8-K — accepted at 08:41 ET (corrected 08-18 from 04:41; see 🔄 Map changes) filed alongside the Ohio press release that this morning's pass read instead — caps the company's obligation at $105 billion and describes an instrument materially different from the "guarantee" the coverage implied. It is a residual-value guarantee on OpenAI's 20-year leases: NVIDIA pays the shortfall between a guaranteed minimum lease value and whatever the site fetches on re-lease or sale, triggered by OpenAI's insolvency or non-payment, attaching only from 2028. And OpenAI has "agreed to reimburse and indemnify NVIDIA for any and all amounts actually paid" — the recourse runs back to the party whose insolvency is the trigger, which means the indemnity is worth least exactly when it is called. The four-number progression this map has tracked since 07-27 closes here: $250B → up to $750B → under $120B (press) → $105B, filed.
